Today, we share the tech report for SmolVLM: Redefining small and efficient multimodal models.
🔥 Explaining how to design a tiny 256M VLM that uses less than 1GB of RAM and outperforms our 80B models from 18 months ago!
Here are the coolest insights from our experiments:
✨ Longer context = Big wins: Increasing the context length from 2K to 16K gave our tiny VLMs a 60% performance boost!
✨ Smaller is smarter with SigLIP: Surprise! Smaller LLMs didn't benefit from the usual large SigLIP (400M). Instead, we use the 80M base SigLIP that performs equally well at just 20% of the original size!
✨ Pixel shuffling magic: Aggressively pixel shuffling helped our compact VLMs "see" better, achieving the same performance with sequences 16x shorter!
✨ Learned positional tokens FTW: For compact models, learned positional tokens significantly outperform raw text tokens, enhancing efficiency and accuracy.
✨ System prompts and special tokens are key: Introducing system prompts and dedicated media intro/outro tokens significantly boosted our compact VLM’s performance—especially for video tasks.
✨ Less CoT, more efficiency: Turns out, too much Chain-of-Thought (CoT) data actually hurts performance in small models. They dumb
✨ Longer videos, better results: Increasing video length during training enhanced performance on both video and image tasks.
🌟 State-of-the-Art Performance, SmolVLM comes in three powerful yet compact sizes—256M, 500M, and 2.2B parameters—each setting new SOTA benchmarks for their hardware constraints in image and video understanding.
📱 Real-world Efficiency: We've created an app using SmolVLM on an iPhone 15 and got real-time inference directly from its camera!

title: steven (@Tu7uruu)
summary:
new Ministral 3 tech report from @MistralAI, they train competitive small models on 1/3T tokens only. the secret? pruning + distillation
distillation:
> in pre-training they use Mistral Small 3.1 Instruct as a teacher for ALL variants (so not really cascade distillation, each smaller model is pruned from the previous one but they all learn from the same teacher). for post training they saw a boost by using Medium 3 (larger model) for SFT, for the reasoning variant, they use Magistral Small for the 3B model. they don't do reverse KL or top-k compression of logits it seems (gemma uses those tricks iirc), just forward KL
> they have a cool ablation showing using instruct model is better than base for STEM, and another one showing that you get a teacher/student gap if the model is too big, basically Medium 3 as teacher hurts pretraining vs Small 3.1 but helps post training. the size of Medium 3 is unknown so a bit hard to draw exact conclusions here..
pruning:
> they prune everything, depth, model dim and ffn dim:
- layer pruning they compute the ratio between the norm of the output and input, if output is similar to input the layer isn't transforming much so you can remove it
- hidden dim they do PCA to find the directions with most variance across all layernorm activations, then prune the low variance ones. the idea is that important features aren't axis-aligned so you need to rotate first before you can prune cleanly
- ffn dim pruning is by looking at the gated activation score (value * gate), they remove neurons where the gate suppresses the value even if the value itself is high
a few points that imo are worth exploring further:
> for layer pruning, nvidia Minitron tried using ppl (and accuracy on downstream task iirc) to see the impact of removing a layer. mistral's norm ratio is simpler but one edge case i can see is like if you have proper feature learning (with like muP) the output/input ratio would not be informative enough? not sure about this
> for pruning an important thing is to use the proper data to compute the importance ratio, would be curious if the data they use here is the same as the training mixture or something more curated
not the distillation part but they use online DPO which seems to be a big deal for alignment bench (even after the RL checkpoint). they sample responses on the fly from current policy and use a pairwise reward model with soft labels instead of hard win/lose
kudos to mistral research team, the paper is nice and has ablations which i think researchers will appreciate a lot!
